audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Leviticus / Vayiqra skin/scale affliction diagnostic text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for tzaraat/scale disease diagnostics, priestly inspection, quarantine, clean/unclean declarations, garments, and outside-camp status. Strong anti-stigma safeguards required.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron, saying,

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: When a human has in skin of flesh a swelling, scab, or bright spot, and it becomes in skin of flesh an affliction of scale-disease/tzaraat, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.

familiar.text: When a man shall have in the skin of his flesh a rising, a scab, or bright spot, and it be in the skin of his flesh like the plague of leprosy; then he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest, or unto one of his sons the priests:

modern.text: “When someone has a swelling or rash or bright spot on his skin that could become an infectious skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.

original.text: אָדָ֗ם כִּֽי יִהְיֶ֤ה בְעוֹר בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ שְׂאֵ֤ת אֽוֹ סַפַּ֨חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַהֶ֔רֶת וְהָיָ֥ה בְעוֹר בְּשָׂר֖וֹ לְנֶ֣גַע צָרָ֑עַת וְהוּבָא֙ אֶל אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֔ן א֛וֹ אֶל אַחַ֥ד מִבָּנָ֖יו הַכֹּהֲנִֽים

verses.restored: The priest shall look at the affliction in skin of flesh; if hair in affliction has turned white and appearance of affliction is deeper than skin of flesh, it is affliction of scale-disease. Priest shall look and declare him unclean.

familiar.text: And the priest shall look on the plague in the skin of the flesh: and when the hair in the plague is turned white, and the plague in sight be deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is a plague of leprosy: and the priest shall look on him, and pronounce him unclean.

modern.text: The priest is to examine the infection on his skin, and if the hair in the infection has turned white and the sore appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.

original.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֣ן אֶת הַנֶּ֣גַע בְּעֽוֹר הַ֠בָּשָׂר וְשֵׂעָ֨ר בַּנֶּ֜גַע הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֗ן וּמַרְאֵ֤ה הַנֶּ֨גַע֙ עָמֹק֙ מֵע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת ה֑וּא וְרָאָ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְטִמֵּ֥א אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: If bright spot is white in skin of flesh and its appearance is not deeper than skin, and its hair has not turned white, priest shall shut up affliction seven days.

familiar.text: If the bright spot be white in the skin of his flesh, and in sight be not deeper than the skin, and the hair thereof be not turned white; then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague seven days:

modern.text: If, however, the spot on his skin is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.

original.text: וְאִם בַּהֶרֶת֩ לְבָנָ֨ה הִ֜וא בְּע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֗וֹ וְעָמֹק֙ אֵין מַרְאֶ֣הָ מִן הָע֔וֹר וּשְׂעָרָ֖ה לֹא הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֑ן וְהִסְגִּ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת הַנֶּ֖גַע שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים

verses.restored: Priest shall look at him on seventh day; if affliction stayed in his eyes and affliction has not spread in skin, priest shall shut him up seven days a second time.

familiar.text: And the priest shall look on him the seventh day: and, behold, if the plague in his sight be at a stay, and the plague spread not in the skin; then the priest shall shut him up seven days more:

modern.text: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if he sees that the infection is unchanged and has not spread on the skin, the priest must isolate him for another seven days.

original.text: וְרָאָ֣הוּ הַכֹּהֵן֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנֶּ֨גַע֙ עָמַ֣ד בְּעֵינָ֔יו לֹֽא פָשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖גַע בָּע֑וֹר וְהִסְגִּיר֧וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית

verses.restored: Priest shall look at him on seventh day a second time; if affliction has faded and has not spread in skin, priest shall declare him clean; it is scab. He shall wash garments and be clean.

familiar.text: And the priest shall look on him again the seventh day: and, behold, if the plague be somewhat dark, and the plague spread not in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean: it is but a scab: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean.

modern.text: The priest will examine him again on the seventh day, and if the sore has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash. The person must wash his clothes and be clean.

original.text: וְרָאָה֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן אֹת֜וֹ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֮ שֵׁנִית֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ כֵּהָ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע וְלֹא פָשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖גַע בָּע֑וֹר וְטִהֲר֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ מִסְפַּ֣חַת הִ֔יא וְכִבֶּ֥ס בְּגָדָ֖יו וְטָהֵֽר

verses.restored: But if scab spreads in skin after he showed himself to priest for cleansing, he shall show himself to priest a second time.

familiar.text: But if the scab spread much abroad in the skin, after that he hath been seen of the priest for his cleansing, he shall be seen of the priest again:

modern.text: But if the rash spreads further on his skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he must present himself again to the priest.

original.text: וְאִם פָּשֹׂ֨ה תִפְשֶׂ֤ה הַמִּסְפַּ֨חַת֙ בָּע֔וֹר אַחֲרֵ֧י הֵרָאֹת֛וֹ אֶל הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לְטָהֳרָת֑וֹ וְנִרְאָ֥ה שֵׁנִ֖ית אֶל הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: Priest shall look, and if scab has spread in skin, priest shall declare him unclean; it is scale-disease.

familiar.text: And if the priest see that, behold, the scab spreadeth in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a leprosy.

modern.text: The priest will reexamine him, and if the rash has spread on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; he has a skin disease.

original.text: וְרָאָה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה פָּשְׂתָ֥ה הַמִּסְפַּ֖חַת בָּע֑וֹר וְטִמְּא֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן צָרַ֥עַת הִֽוא

verses.restored: When affliction of scale-disease is in a human, he shall be brought to priest.

familiar.text: When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought unto the priest;

modern.text: When anyone develops a skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.

original.text: נֶ֣גַע צָרַ֔עַת כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה בְּאָדָ֑ם וְהוּבָ֖א אֶל הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: Priest shall look, and if there is white swelling in skin, and it has turned hair white, and living raw flesh in swelling,

familiar.text: And the priest shall see him: and, behold, if the rising be white in the skin, and it have turned the hair white, and there be quick raw flesh in the rising;

modern.text: The priest will examine him, and if there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,

original.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה שְׂאֵת לְבָנָה֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְהִ֕יא הָפְכָ֖ה שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֑ן וּמִֽחְיַ֛ת בָּשָׂ֥ר חַ֖י בַּשְׂאֵֽת

verses.restored: it is chronic scale-disease in skin of flesh, and priest shall declare him unclean; he shall not shut him up, for he is unclean.

familiar.text: It is an old leprosy in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean, and shall not shut him up: for he is unclean.

modern.text: it is a chronic skin disease and the priest must pronounce him unclean. He need not isolate him, for he is unclean.

original.text: צָרַ֨עַת נוֹשֶׁ֤נֶת הִוא֙ בְּע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וְטִמְּא֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן לֹ֣א יַסְגִּרֶ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י טָמֵ֖א הֽוּא

verses.restored: If scale-disease breaks out in skin, and scale-disease covers all skin of afflicted one from head to feet, everywhere eyes of priest see,

familiar.text: And if a leprosy break out abroad in the skin, and the leprosy cover all the skin of him that hath the plague from his head even to his foot, wheresoever the priest looketh;

modern.text: But if the skin disease breaks out all over his skin so that it covers all the skin of the infected person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,

original.text: וְאִם פָּר֨וֹחַ תִּפְרַ֤ח הַצָּרַ֨עַת֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְכִסְּתָ֣ה הַצָּרַ֗עַת אֵ֚ת כָּל ע֣וֹר הַנֶּ֔גַע מֵרֹאשׁ֖וֹ וְעַד רַגְלָ֑יו לְכָל מַרְאֵ֖ה עֵינֵ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: then priest shall look, and if scale-disease covers all his flesh, he shall declare afflicted one clean; all of it has turned white; he is clean.

familiar.text: Then the priest shall consider: and, behold, if the leprosy have covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague: it is all turned white: he is clean.

modern.text: the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has covered his entire body, he is to pronounce the infected person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.

original.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֨ה כִסְּתָ֤ה הַצָּרַ֨עַת֙ אֶת כָּל בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וְטִהַ֖ר אֶת הַנָּ֑גַע כֻּלּ֛וֹ הָפַ֥ךְ לָבָ֖ן טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא

verses.restored: But on day raw flesh appears in him, he shall be unclean.

familiar.text: But when raw flesh appeareth in him, he shall be unclean.

modern.text: But whenever raw flesh appears on someone, he will be unclean.

original.text: וּבְי֨וֹם הֵרָא֥וֹת בּ֛וֹ בָּשָׂ֥ר חַ֖י יִטְמָֽא

verses.restored: Priest shall look at raw flesh and declare him unclean; raw flesh is unclean; it is scale-disease.

familiar.text: And the priest shall see the raw flesh, and pronounce him to be unclean: for the raw flesh is unclean: it is a leprosy.

modern.text: When the priest sees the raw flesh, he must pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a skin disease.

original.text: וְרָאָ֧ה הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֖י וְטִמְּא֑וֹ הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֛י טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא צָרַ֥עַת הֽוּא

verses.restored: Or if raw flesh turns again and becomes white, he shall come to priest.

familiar.text: Or if the raw flesh turn again, and be changed unto white, he shall come unto the priest;

modern.text: But if the raw flesh changes and turns white, he must go to the priest.

original.text: א֣וֹ כִ֥י יָשׁ֛וּב הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֖י וְנֶהְפַּ֣ךְ לְלָבָ֑ן וּבָ֖א אֶל הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: Priest shall look at him, and if affliction turned white, priest shall declare afflicted one clean; he is clean.

familiar.text: And the priest shall see him: and, behold, if the plague be turned into white; then the priest shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague: he is clean.

modern.text: The priest will reexamine him, and if the infection has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the infected person clean; then he is clean.

original.text: וְרָאָ֨הוּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ הַנֶּ֖גַע לְלָבָ֑ן וְטִהַ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת הַנֶּ֖גַע טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא

verses.restored: When flesh has in its skin a boil and it is healed,

familiar.text: The flesh also, in which, even in the skin thereof, was a boil, and is healed,

modern.text: When a boil appears on someone’s skin and it heals,

original.text: וּבָשָׂ֕ר כִּֽי יִהְיֶ֥ה בֽוֹ בְעֹר֖וֹ שְׁחִ֑ין וְנִרְפָּֽא

verses.restored: and in place of boil there is white swelling or reddish-white bright spot, it shall be shown to priest.

familiar.text: And in the place of the boil there be a white rising, or a bright spot, white, and somewhat reddish, and it be shewed to the priest;

modern.text: and a white swelling or a reddish-white spot develops where the boil was, he must present himself to the priest.

original.text: וְהָיָ֞ה בִּמְק֤וֹם הַשְּׁחִין֙ שְׂאֵ֣ת לְבָנָ֔ה א֥וֹ בַהֶ֖רֶת לְבָנָ֣ה אֲדַמְדָּ֑מֶת וְנִרְאָ֖ה אֶל הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: Priest shall look, and if its appearance is lower than skin and its hair turned white, priest shall declare him unclean; it is affliction of scale-disease broken out in boil.

familiar.text: And if, when the priest seeth it, behold, it be in sight lower than the skin, and the hair thereof be turned white; the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a plague of leprosy broken out of the boil.

modern.text: The priest shall examine it, and if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection that has broken out in the boil.

original.text: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה מַרְאֶ֨הָ֙ שָׁפָ֣ל מִן הָע֔וֹר וּשְׂעָרָ֖הּ הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֑ן וְטִמְּא֧וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן נֶֽגַע צָרַ֥עַת הִ֖וא בַּשְּׁחִ֥ין פָּרָֽחָה

verses.restored: But if priest looks, and there is no white hair in it and it is not lower than skin and it has faded, priest shall shut him up seven days.

familiar.text: But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no white hairs therein, and if it be not lower than the skin, but be somewhat dark; then the priest shall shut him up seven days:

modern.text: But when the priest examines it, if there is no white hair in it, and it is not beneath the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.

original.text: וְאִ֣ם יִרְאֶ֣נָּה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין בָּהּ֙ שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֔ן וּשְׁפָלָ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נָּה מִן הָע֖וֹר וְהִ֣יא כֵהָ֑ה וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים

verses.restored: If spreading, it spreads in skin, priest shall declare him unclean; it is affliction.

familiar.text: And if it spread much abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a plague.

modern.text: If it spreads any further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is an infection.

original.text: וְאִם פָּשֹׂ֥ה תִפְשֶׂ֖ה בָּע֑וֹר וְטִמֵּ֧א הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֹת֖וֹ נֶ֥גַע הִֽוא

verses.restored: But if bright spot remains in its place and has not spread, it is scar of boil; priest shall declare him clean.

familiar.text: But if the bright spot stay in his place, and spread not, it is a burning boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.

modern.text: But if the spot remains unchanged and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.

original.text: וְאִם תַּחְתֶּ֜יהָ תַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַבַּהֶ֨רֶת֙ לֹ֣א פָשָׂ֔תָה צָרֶ֥בֶת הַשְּׁחִ֖ין הִ֑וא וְטִהֲר֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: Or when flesh has in its skin burn from fire, and living part of burn becomes reddish-white or white bright spot,

familiar.text: Or if there be any flesh, in the skin whereof there is a hot burning, and the quick flesh that burneth have a white bright spot, somewhat reddish, or white;

modern.text: When there is a burn on someone’s skin and the raw area of the burn becomes reddish-white or white,

verses.restored: priest shall look at it; if hair in bright spot turned white and its appearance is deeper than skin, it is scale-disease broken out in burn; priest shall declare him unclean; it is affliction of scale-disease.

familiar.text: Then the priest shall look upon it: and, behold, if the hair in the bright spot be turned white, and it be in sight deeper than the skin; it is a leprosy broken out of the burning: wherefore the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy.

modern.text: the priest must examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.

verses.restored: But if priest looks, and there is no white hair in bright spot and it is not lower than skin and has faded, priest shall shut him up seven days.

familiar.text: But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no white hair in the bright spot, and it be no lower than the other skin, but be somewhat dark; then the priest shall shut him up seven days:

modern.text: But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not beneath the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.

verses.restored: Priest shall look at him on seventh day; if spreading, it spreads in skin, priest shall declare him unclean; it is affliction of scale-disease.

verses.restored: priest shall command that they wash what has affliction, and he shall shut it up seven days a second time.

familiar.text: Then the priest shall command that they wash the thing wherein the plague is, and he shall shut it up seven days more:

modern.text: the priest is to order the contaminated article to be washed and isolated for another seven days.

original.text: וְצִוָּה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְכִ֨בְּס֔וּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר בּ֖וֹ הַנָּ֑גַע וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ שִׁבְעַת יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית

verses.restored: Priest shall look after affliction is washed; if affliction has not changed its appearance and affliction has not spread, it is unclean; in fire you shall burn it, whether decay is on bare side or front.

familiar.text: And the priest shall look on the plague, after that it is washed: and, behold, if the plague have not changed his colour, and the plague be not spread; it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire; it is fret inward, whether it be bare within or without.

modern.text: After it has been washed, the priest is to reexamine it, and if the mildewed article has not changed in appearance, it is unclean. Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back.

original.text: וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אַחֲרֵ֣י הֻכַּבֵּ֣ס אֶת הַנֶּ֗גַע וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹֽא הָפַ֨ךְ הַנֶּ֤גַע אֶת עֵינוֹ֙ וְהַנֶּ֣גַע לֹֽא פָשָׂ֔ה טָמֵ֣א ה֔וּא בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶ֑נּוּ פְּחֶ֣תֶת הִ֔וא בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֥וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: But if priest looks, and affliction has faded after washing it, he shall tear it from garment or skin, from warp or woof.

familiar.text: And if the priest look, and, behold, the plague be somewhat dark after the washing of it; then he shall rend it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof:

modern.text: If the priest examines it and the mildew has faded after it has been washed, he must cut the contaminated section out of the fabric, leather, weave, or knit.

original.text: וְאִם֮ רָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ כֵּהָ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע אַחֲרֵ֖י הֻכַּבֵּ֣ס אֹת֑וֹ וְקָרַ֣ע אֹת֗וֹ מִן הַבֶּ֨גֶד֙ א֣וֹ מִן הָע֔וֹר א֥וֹ מִן הַשְּׁתִ֖י א֥וֹ מִן הָעֵֽרֶב

verses.restored: If it appears again in garment, warp or woof, or any vessel of skin, it is outbreak; in fire you shall burn what has affliction.

familiar.text: And if it appear still in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; it is a spreading plague: thou shalt burn that wherein the plague is with fire.

modern.text: But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.

original.text: וְאִם תֵּרָאֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד בַּ֠בֶּגֶד אֽוֹ בַשְּׁתִ֤י אֽוֹ בָעֵ֨רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְכָל כְּלִי ע֔וֹר פֹּרַ֖חַת הִ֑וא בָּאֵ֣שׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶ֔נּוּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר בּ֖וֹ הַנָּֽגַע

verses.restored: Garment, warp or woof, or any vessel of skin that you wash and affliction turns aside from them shall be washed a second time and be clean.

familiar.text: And the garment, either warp, or woof, or whatsoever thing of skin it be, which thou shalt wash, if the plague be departed from them, then it shall be washed the second time, and shall be clean.

modern.text: If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean.

original.text: וְהַבֶּ֡גֶד אֽוֹ הַשְּׁתִ֨י אוֹ הָעֵ֜רֶב אֽוֹ כָל כְּלִ֤י הָעוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תְּכַבֵּ֔ס וְסָ֥ר מֵהֶ֖ם הַנָּ֑גַע וְכֻבַּ֥ס שֵׁנִ֖ית וְטָהֵֽר

verses.restored: This is Torah/instruction of affliction of scale-disease in garment of wool or linen, or warp or woof, or any vessel of skin, to declare it clean or to declare it unclean.

familiar.text: This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment of woollen or linen, either in the warp, or woof, or any thing of skins, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.

modern.text: This is the law concerning a mildew contamination in wool or linen fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article, for pronouncing it clean or unclean.”

original.text: זֹ֠את תּוֹרַ֨ת נֶֽגַע צָרַ֜עַת בֶּ֥גֶד הַצֶּ֣מֶר א֣וֹ הַפִּשְׁתִּ֗ים א֤וֹ הַשְּׁתִי֙ א֣וֹ הָעֵ֔רֶב א֖וֹ כָּל כְּלִי ע֑וֹר לְטַהֲר֖וֹ א֥וֹ לְטַמְּאֽוֹ

translation_notes: Tzaraat is not modern leprosy/Hansen's disease by default; render as scale-disease/skin affliction pending lexical audit.
Priest functions diagnostically/ritually, not as moral accuser.
Quarantine and outside-camp status are ritual/community protection measures; do not use for stigma or dehumanization.
Many conditions are declared clean; the chapter carefully distinguishes and reinspects rather than assuming uncleanness.
Garment affliction shows category is broader than human disease.
safety_note: Do not use Leviticus 13 to stigmatize illness, skin conditions, disability, baldness, infection, or people outside communal space. This is ancient ritual diagnosis and quarantine language, not a statement of human worth or spiritual contamination.
